title: Artifact retention must protect referenced images
summary: Retention policies must protect images and artifacts still referenced by active services, rollback targets, or recovery plans. Otherwise cleanup breaks rollback during the incident that needs it.
ai_value: Helps agents avoid deleting deploy artifacts that are still part of the live or rollback safety envelope.

contexts: a registry or artifact store retention policy deletes old tags, images, or build artifacts
active services, workload specs, or rollback plans reference immutable artifact digests
cleanup is run before proving referenced artifacts remain available

trigger_signals.description: A retention policy selects artifacts by age or tag count without checking active and rollback references.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Diff references against retained artifacts before applying cleanup.

trigger_signals.description: Rollback instructions name an artifact that may no longer exist in the registry or store.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat rollback as unproven until the referenced artifact is fetched or verified.

trigger_signals.description: Cleanup is bundled with incident recovery or release closeout.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Protect the referenced artifact set before deleting anything.

negative_signals.description: The system has a separately verified immutable artifact archive for rollback.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Retention can be safe when rollback references are protected elsewhere.

negative_signals.description: The artifact is proven unreferenced by live, pending, and rollback targets.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Then cleanup may proceed through the normal safe path.

common_wrong_assumptions: Old tags are safe to delete because current deploy uses the latest tag.
Rollback plans are valid even if the referenced artifact was garbage-collected.
Registry cleanup is low-risk hygiene during release work.

first_checks.check: List active, pending, and rollback artifact references as immutable digests or exact IDs.
first_checks.why: Tags can move; retention safety needs the actual referenced artifacts.

first_checks.check: Diff the referenced artifact set against registry or artifact-store manifests before and after policy changes.
first_checks.why: This proves retention did not remove safety-critical artifacts.

first_checks.check: Keep cleanup separate from incident rollback unless references are protected.
first_checks.why: Cleanup can destroy the recovery path while trying to tidy it.

decision_rules.condition: Retention would delete an active, pending, or rollback-referenced artifact.
decision_rules.then: Do not apply retention until the reference is moved, archived, or explicitly retired.

decision_rules.condition: References are protected and dry-run shows only unreferenced artifacts removed.
decision_rules.then: Proceed with cleanup under the normal change path and keep manifest evidence.

decision_rules.condition: Rollback artifact availability is unknown during an incident.
decision_rules.then: Fetch or inspect the artifact reference before relying on rollback.

do_not: Do not delete artifacts by age alone when live or rollback references exist.
Do not assume tags are stable rollback evidence.
Do not publish private registry names, deployment identifiers, or internal handoff pointers in the record.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Before artifact retention cleanup, diff active and rollback references against the artifacts that the policy will keep.

risk.notes: This record is de-identified agent guidance. It does not authorize bypassing maintainer, security, publication, production, billing, data, permission, or destructive-action gates.
